definition: Token-level routing over depth: each layer processes only a routed subset of tokens, so easy tokens skip compute.
details: Token-level routing over depth: each layer processes only a routed subset of tokens, so easy tokens skip compute. The depth-wise complement to Mixture of Experts' width-wise routing, part of the broader conditional computation program.

explainer.lead: Mixture of Depths routes tokens over depth so each layer processes only a routed subset of tokens and easy tokens skip compute. It matters as the depth-wise complement to Mixture of Experts' width-wise routing within conditional computation.

tiers.eli5: Some words in a sentence are easy, so the model lets them skip ahead while spending effort only on the tricky ones.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use token-level routing to save compute per layer without shrinking the model; a pitfall is router imbalance or dropped information if routing is poorly tuned.
tiers.paperLevel: Each layer processes only a routed subset of tokens, so easy tokens skip compute; it is token-level routing over depth, complementing MoE's width-wise routing.

explainer.example: In a long prompt, common filler tokens exit early at shallow layers while ambiguous tokens continue through deeper layers.
